links.title: Dashing Commander (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: An inspiration on the battlefield, a dashing commander uses her potent battle cries to inspire her allies and lead them to victory.

links.title: Flying Blade (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: Rather than fighting in the fray, a flying blade swashbuckler focuses on combat from afar using an array of dazzling attacks with thrown weapons rather than sully herself with the blood of her enemies.

links.title: Gallivant (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: Rather than getting bogged down in a fray, a gallivant dashes into combat atop a loyal steed, sweeping hither and yon with flashing blade and lashing hooves and leaving broken bones and broken hearts in her wake.

links.title: Heightened Blade (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)

links.title: Inspired Blade (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: An inspired blade is both a force of personality and a sage of swordplay dedicated to the perfection of combat with the rapier . They use the science and geometry with swordplay to beautiful and deadly effect.

links.title: Mouser (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: In the hands of a trained warrior, a well-sharpened blade is deadly regardless of size. A mouser moves in close, using her size and skill as an advantage.

links.title: Musketeer (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: Musketeers are brave (or foolish) swashbucklers who wield firearms with reckless abandon on the battlefield. Favored by swaths of organizations and kingdoms, a musketeer’s daring nature makes him ideal for the high-risk, high-reward gamble…

links.title: Mysterious Avenger (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: While some swashbucklers fight for queen and country, and others for coin, glory, or just the enhancement of their own reputations, the mysterious avenger fights directly for a cause. Instead of gaining personal glory for her heroic deeds,…

links.title: Picaroon (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: While some swashbucklers take pride in their ability to wear down an opponent with great skill at arms and clever positioning, a picaroon relies on her firearms to get in close and hit hard.

links.title: Rapscallion (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: Though no less a braggart compared to other swashbucklers, a rapscallion forgoes any semblance of honor in favor of dastardly tricks and surprise assaults against unprepared foes.

links.title: Ronin (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: A ronin is a lordless swordsman, sometimes called a knight-errant. Although most ronin seek a new master to restore their honor, others stick to the lordless lifestyle for personal reasons.

links.title: Tumbler (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: A master of mobility, a tumbler gracefully darts her way across the battlefield, weaving between her opponents in order to gain the perfect vantage point from which to strike.

links.title: Two-Weapon Duelist (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: Although most swashbucklers fight using the free-hand style, a two-weapon warrior favors wielding two weapons at once.

links.title: Vainglorious Swashbuckler (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: The vainglory swashbuckler is a master of her panache, using it to perform superhuman stunts at a moment’s notice.

links.title: Whirling Dervish (Legendary Swashbuckler Archetype)
links.snippet: Some warriors have adapted dances into graceful martial forms, and their swashbuckling style is feared throughout the world its ability to devastate foes with a scimitar through motion and agility regardless of strength of arms.

links.title: Braggart (Swashbuckler Personage)
links.snippet: Although they come in very different shapes, styles, and temperaments, all swashbucklers with the braggart personage are united by their larger-than-life egos and their uncanny ability to crush their opponents’ spirit through sheer force…

links.title: Dandy (Swashbuckler Personage)

links.title: Daredevil (Swashbuckler Personage)
links.snippet: Ever-ready to charge headfirst into trouble, a swashbuckler with the daredevil personage is fast on her feet and more than willing to meet trouble with the edge of her blade.

links.title: Madcap (Swashbuckler Personage)
links.snippet: Although all swashbucklers are somewhat reckless, a madcap epitomizes the reckless flair that characterizes panache users. Fearless before danger by spell or by blade, a madcap is staunch in her resolve and tireless in her pursuits.

links.title: Phantom (Swashbuckler Personage)

links.title: Raider (Swashbuckler Personage)

links.title: Vagabond (Swashbuckler Personage)
links.snippet: Masters of dirty fighting and gang-up tactics, vagabond swashbucklers use their impressive swordplay and flair to strike telling blows upon their rivals when they are least prepared for them.

links.snippet: The most powerful weapon can be the faithful themselves.

links.snippet: The shield bearer is like a rock in the river of battle, standing strong as the water breaks around it. They hold their shield as a divine bulwark defending them and sending their foes scattering in the face of its might.

links.snippet: The Daughters of the Raging Storm are a cult devoted to the power and majesty of storm spirits, gods of the sky, and the powers of lightning, wind, and rain.

links.title: Heaven of Blood War

links.title: Artillerist (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: Artillerists provide long range support and lead from the back, ensuring victory by striking at the right moment.

links.title: Banneret (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: The banneret is a marshal who has many other warriors under their banner. They are accompanied by their standard-bearer and eventually, a full retinue.

links.title: Chevalier (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: Some marshals know that being able to cross the battlefield can grant more heart to your allies than leading from one position.

links.title: Dashing Champion (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: These marshals lead by example, not by mentoring and supporting directly, but inspiring through their own exemplary exploits.

links.title: Dauntless Juggernaut (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: Some marshals become infamous as immortal generals or insurmountable obstacles. Inspiring others by absorbing blows that may kill lesser beings.

links.title: Dragon Shaman (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: Dragon shamans are marshals who derive their leadership skills and powers from their association or kinship with dragons.

links.title: Faithful Adjutant (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: These marshals eschew tactics and combat alone and attune themselves to higher faiths, deities, or other philosophies. They then share this with their allies to bolster their bonds and bodies alike.

links.title: Harsh Mentor (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: While often rough around the edges, these marshals keep their comrades in shape and support them with devastating unarmed strikes.

links.title: Marquis (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: These marshals do battle in a different theater altogether, that of the noble court. Trading some of their martial leadership for a silvered tongue and a honeyed word or knife in the back.

links.title: Nature’s Vanguard (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: No matter the state of things, nature often needs a champion to defend it and these marshals accept that honor. They fight not for the armies of civilization, but lead animals and the people of the unconquered lands.

links.title: Raid Leader (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: Even unorganized forces can create worthy leaders. The raid leader turns battle by virtue of overwhelming force, always being the first into the fray.

links.title: Warlord (Marshal Archetype)
links.snippet: Some marshals devote themselves to the art of combat and inspiring their allies on the front-line at a deeper level than other marshals.

links.title: Bounty Hunter (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Wherever there are bounties to be claimed, there are always those who will come to claim them.

links.title: Brutish Guide (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Some scouts are closer to barbarians in demeanor, using great strength and intimidation to contend with wild places.

links.title: Cavalry Scout (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Most scouts are too slow on foot to scout large open areas, or against fast-moving enemies. This is where the cavalry scout and their mount come in.

links.title: Crossbow Champion (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: The crossbow is an under-loved weapon. In the right hands it becomes a formidable and versatile tool.

links.title: Dagger Master (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Dagger masters hone their craft with short blades beyond the skill of all but the most specialized combatants.

links.title: Disciple of the Bow (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Disciples of the bow treat archery as a precise and deadly art form.

links.title: Horizon Sniper (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Horizon Snipers train to strike even the furthest enemies with precision.

links.title: Packmaster (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Some scouts work in tandem with trained beasts.

links.title: Phase Striker (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Scouts are already masters of mobility, these scouts take it even further, flitting from place to place by teleporting.

links.title: Rugged Detective (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Scouts sometimes operate in urban environments where their skills and mobility can make them excellent investigators and spies.

links.title: Swordlord Dancer (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Among the many masters of sword dueling, the swordlords are one of the well known schools. There is a subset that learns a cultural sword dance that was derived from the fighting style. These dancers are fluid movers, mobile, and masters…

links.title: Tracker (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Trackers refocus some of their subterfuge skills into tracking their enemies and game while in the wilds.

links.title: Trickshot Champion (Scout Archetype)
links.snippet: Trickshot champions take pride in their work, often more haughty and boisterous than other scouts. Showmanship empowers their dazzling throwing techniques.

links.title: Arcane Ace
links.snippet: Some dealers can use legerdemain in their card skills, others actually infuse their card skill with arcane energies.

links.title: Luckmaker
links.snippet: Most dealers have luck and skill that help them in their craft, luckmakers make their own luck to stack the deck in their favor.

links.title: Black Arrow (Lathspell Archetype)
links.snippet: A black arrow is proficient in all simple weapons and martial weapons and light armor. Black arrows are not proficient with shields.

links.title: Corrupted Avenger (Lathspell Archetype)
links.snippet: A corrupted avenger does not gain spells.

links.title: Martyred Soul (Lathspell Archetype)
links.snippet: A martyred soul casts divine spells drawn from the paladin spell list instead of the normal lathspell spell list.

links.title: Curse of Altered Perceptions
links.snippet: Bonus Spells : 0th — ghost sound , 1st — illusion of calm , 2nd — mirror image , 3rd — major image , 4th — phantasmal killer

links.title: Curse of Altered Perceptions
links.snippet: Bonus Spells : 0th — ghost sound , 1st — illusion of calm , 2nd — mirror image , 3rd — major image , 4th — phantasmal killer

links.title: Curse of Death
links.snippet: The reaper’s grasp is cold and inevitable.

links.title: Curse of Entropy
links.snippet: Bonus Spells : 0th — touch of fatigue , 1st — break , 2nd —diminish resistance , 3rd — rusting grasp , 4th —rune of ruin

links.title: Curse of Misfortune
links.snippet: Bonus Spells : 0th —chance*, 1st — compel hostility , 2nd — locate weakness , 3rd — screech , 4th —pessimism

links.title: Curse of Mutable Form
links.snippet: Flesh is malleable but sometimes an overindulgence in the change makes it difficult to return to normal.

links.title: Curse of Pain
links.snippet: All existence is pain. You cannot escape it, so use it instead.

links.title: Curse of the Hungering Blade (Lathspell Curse)
links.snippet: The moment your hand touched the weapon, its fate became yours.

links.title: Curse of the Wilds
links.snippet: Every untamed land is home to wild things.

links.title: Curse of Violence
links.snippet: Bonus Spells : 0th — bleed , 1st — lead blades , 2nd — rage , 3rd — keen edge , 4th — stoneskin

links.title: Dishonored
links.snippet: A dishonored is a vanguard that eschews their code and their responsibilities and can be the bane of the protectors of the realm or simply errant warriors selling their skills to the highest bidder.

links.title: Immerhalm
links.snippet: An immerhalm is a vanguard that realizes that sometimes the best defense is a good offence. What better way to defend their allies than with a big hammer, axe or sword?

links.title: Mercenary Captain
links.snippet: A mercenary captain can be a leader of thugs or a more righteous band, but they always do whatever necessary to complete their goals and ensure that jobs are always fruitful for their squad.

links.title: Swordlord Guardian
links.snippet: Dueling schools are known for putting out skilled warriors. Some, while trained to be excellent duelists, are also trained to be nimble bodyguards and protectors. These are the swordlord guardians, master of using the blade to keep their…

links.title: Templar
links.snippet: In the religious orders of the world, there are the priests and clerics which are the head and face of the religion.

links.title: Arcane Bomber (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: An arcane bomber learns techniques to instill magic into physical bombs they can use on the battlefield.

links.title: Arcane Destroyer (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: An arcane destroyer uses fury to power their spells, as reckless as that may be. They are devastating on the battlefield, but can be an easy target by their enemies seeking to stymy the pure destruction they bring. They are not strategic,…

links.title: Arcane Shield (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: Some warmages delve deeply into abjuration magic to protect their allies on the battlefield. These are the arcane shields.

links.title: Battlefield Caller (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: Some warmages focus their leaning upon calling, summoning, and creating their weapons. These are called the battlefield callers.

links.title: Bladebound Warmage (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: Some warmages are chosen to bear the black blade-a sentient weapon of often unknown and possibly unknowable purpose. Who chose them or why is a mystery, but the black blade is a powerful tool. As a black blade becomes more aware, its true…

links.title: City Magi (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: You have sworn to protect the citizenry of your district, gaining power and influence from your commitment to the welfare of the community and upholding its laws.

links.title: Holy Warmage (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: Sometimes divine magic is insufficient in the divine struggles that bleed over into the mortal planes. In steps the holy warmage, an arcane sword in the hands of their faith.

links.title: Instructor (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: The war colleges that instruct warmages need people to teach others in their craft. This is where the instructor comes in.

links.title: Merchant of Doom (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: Merchants of doom are the fear-mongers among warmages trained in the dark warfare of instilling fear, breaking morale, and cursing their opponents. They trade in doom and despair.

links.title: Signifer Warmage (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: The hellknights are a terrible and militant order. While most of their signifers are priests or conjurers, some are trained to be warmages to bring powerful offensive magic to bear on the unlawful.

links.title: Spellslinger (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: The warmage is a master of combat-centric magic and gunners are at the forefront of combat technology. The spellslinger is a warmage that takes their skill in devastating arcane magics and pairs it with guns.

links.title: War Shadow (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: War shadows eschew more of the actively violent spells to use the power of the shadow plane to the battlefield.

links.title: Weapon Binder (Warmage Archetype)
links.snippet: Weapon binders are a specific tradition of warmages that eschew some of their tactical expertise with a deep bond with a weapon that they excel with and that defends them.

links.title: Angelic Choirs Influence
links.snippet: Some mediums develop a connection beyond the material world after a near-death experience gives them a momentary glimpse of the glory of a good deity and their angelic servants. The voices of angels linger in the mind of such mediums, who…

links.title: Diabolical Influence
links.snippet: A diabolical influence most commonly manifests to a youth so obsessed with some project or scheme that she cannot spare time even to sleep for nights on end. If she is destined to be a medium with diabolical influence, she finds visions of…

links.title: Fathomless Influence
links.snippet: A dive into the salty embrace of the dark ocean depths sometimes threatens to crush the mind and soul just as readily as it threatens to force the air from a youth’s lungs. Some mediums survive a harrowing dive (be it from a sinking ship…

links.title: Heavenly Hosts Influence
links.snippet: Individuals that spend long hours in patient meditation occasionally experience a sudden awakening to the wider cosmos in a way that loosens the bonds of mortal perception, allowing them to see as spirits do. The natives of Heaven,…

links.title: Restless Souls Influence
links.snippet: When the death of a very close friend or other loved one threatens to overwhelm a young medium’s mind with bereavement, he may find he attracts the interest of many different restless souls who feel a connection to his sorrow, even long…

links.title: Seelie Court Influence
links.snippet: Those that dally with fey or other magical beings often find themselves the unwitting subjects of hypnotism (magical or mundane). For most, this hypnotic state passes without a trace as soon after the being departs, but for a few, it…

links.title: Smokeborn Influence
links.snippet: Some mediums first glimpse the spirit world through the haze of noxious smoke, poison, or drugs that burn intensely in their minds. These mediums often develop a rapport with fire spirits, whose numbers include the brigidine ( azata ),…

links.title: Stony Silence Influence
links.snippet: Some mediums first become attuned to hearing and seeing things beyond the material world when their senses are deprived of material sights and sounds for a long period of time, such as in the darkness of a cave-in or in a collapse after an…

links.title: Stormbound Influence
links.snippet: Some mediums awaken into their powers after a desperate winter left them starved and delirious enough for their perceptions to mingle the material world with the reality of cold and aerial spirits. The stormbound influence connects these…

links.title: Transformative Influence
links.snippet: Some mediums awaken into their powers after a delirious fever dream or perception-shattering hallucination revealed to them how fragile and changeable physical shapes can be. The transformative influence connects these medium to spirits…

links.title: Unseelie Court Influence
links.snippet: Those that stumble upon areas protected by spiteful fey often suffer from seizures or strokes brought on by foul otherworldly curses. Sometimes, a trespasser finds that while her body and mind are wracked, her perceptions expand painfully,…

links.title: Alchemical Meister (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Although most alchemists seek to use alchemy to ensnare their own magical potential within brews and archaic formulae, alchemical meisters use the alchemical arts to better understand the nature of the spirit realm.

links.title: Eldritch Jailer (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Whether by chance or necessity, some pactmakers are thrown into the world of pact magic when they are forced to act as a jailer of a terrible being from beyond reality, harboring a terrible power that was never meant to be.

links.title: Mad Cultist (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Pactmakers who cannot control their dabbling inevitably plummet too deeply into the shadows of pact magic and emerge as gibbering husks that are little more than puppets of the unknown horrors of the Spirit Realm.

links.title: Occult Scholar (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Referenced throughout occult lore, an occult scholar is any individual who wholly devotes herself to the study of spirits. Occult scholars spend their lives acquiring occult knowledge, often by adventuring out into the world, guided by…

links.title: Prophet (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Although few in number, divine entities that support the practice of pact magic exist in the world. In addition to empowering clerics and other divine servants, these deities call upon practitioners of pact magic to carry out their will,…

links.title: Seal-Etched Pactmaker (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Some pactmakers take to decorating their bodies with the seals of the spirits that they bind, allowing them to quickly seal pacts thanks to their favored seals always being on hand, literally.

links.title: Thaumaturge (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Thaumaturges study the rippling effects that spirit usage has on reality. By doing so, thaumaturges learn how to rip apart the laws of reality in order to achieve fantastic, supernatural results.

links.title: Unbound Pactmaker (Pactmaker Archetype)
links.snippet: Pactmakers who allow spirits unmanaged access to their bodies and souls become physically damned as they mutate into strange, impossible forms. Eventually, these unbound pactmakers lose their ties to their mortality and become little…

links.title: Shaman Elementalist (Elementalist Archetype)
links.snippet: Some elementalists are shamanistic warriors who practice magic and form pacts with the elemental lords of their world. They work closely with actual shamans from their reality, even gathering in a mutual hall at the edge of a dangerous…

links.title: Shugenja (Elementalist Archetype)
links.snippet: The ancient order of Shugenja are sorcerous elementalists who channel their power through harmony with air, earth, fire, and water. They seek balance between the elements and use that balance to create their spells.

links.title: Animal Companion (Trainer Perk)
links.snippet: You gain the animal companion class feature as a druid of your monster trainer level –3. Your animal companion must be an animal you have captured that qualifies to be a druid’s animal companion. When you call upon it as your active…

links.title: Appraise Monster
links.snippet: You can substitute Appraise for any Knowledge skill when making a monster lore check. When you succeed at a monster lore check, you also learn the strength of the monster’s aura (its CR) and current bonus it has (if any) to save against…

links.title: Armored Companion
links.snippet: Your monsters are proficient with the same armor and shields you are. Any armor a monster wears when you recall it falls to the ground where it stood. Wild armor does not fall off in this way.

links.title: Beloved Monster
links.snippet: One non-companion monster of your choice becomes your beloved monster. This monster cannot grow into a stronger form, but its base attack bonus is equal to your monster trainer level, and it adds your Charisma modifier as a morale bonus to…

links.title: Monster Summoning
links.snippet: Requires spell familiarity . You learn the spells summon monster and summon nature’s ally for each spell level you can cast, but you cannot have an active monster while you have one or more creatures summoned in this way. When you cast…

links.title: Run with Me
links.snippet: When you move as a move action, your active monster can also move up to half its speed as part of the same action and vice versa. You can select this perk twice, at which point you and your active monster can move at full speed instead.

links.title: Side-by-Side
links.snippet: For each attack the trainer makes as part of a full attack action , his active monster can also make one attack and vice versa. This does not allow the monster or the trainer to make more attacks than they normally could with a full attack…

links.title: Tough Companion
links.snippet: When you call upon a monster, it appears with hit points equal to your current hit points + your monster trainer level.

links.title: The Monster Within
links.snippet: Prerequisites : 20th level monster trainer, master perk.

links.snippet: S-Class Bloodragers Bloodlines

links.title: Ghost Slayers
links.snippet: The first bloodstalker order to exist was the Ghost Slayers, who originated as an order of fallen paladins hell-bent on continuing their crusade with or without the backing of their gods. They are credited with the discovery of the…

links.title: Moonguard
links.snippet: A relatively new band of bloodstalkers, the moonguard formed to pose a challenge to the rising number of lycanthropes , fey , and other shapechangers after the war against the Chaos. Their silver blades are as dangerous as their…

links.title: Outer Realm
links.snippet: Bloodstalkers of the Order of the Outer Realm deal with monsters and mutations that exist beyond reality and the realms of sanity. They emphasize battle against aberrations and monstrous humanoids . Most who join this order are fey…

links.title: Perfected
links.snippet: The Perfected are an order of bloodstalkers who believe their given forms are nothing more than a starting point from which they can improve and eventually become the most efficient of their kind. They study the creation of constructs and…

links.title: Self-Taught Brawler (S-Class Brawler Archetype)
links.snippet: Self-taught brawlers are those who trade some of their flexibility with feats for more formalized armor and weapon training. They might have read of the exploits of a wandering master, joined a militia with no regiment of its own, or…

links.title: Contract S-Class Inquisition
links.snippet: As a contract inquisitor, you have been hired by the church of another deity to track and deal with heretics as well as other creatures that may challenge your contractor’s faith.

links.title: Alchemical Science
links.snippet: Alchemical science is the traditional practice of many standard s-class investigators, and s-class investigators are just as likely to take it up to help themselves and, in some cases, allies in the heat of battle.

links.title: Brohk
links.snippet: The Brohk methodology was named for a lizardfolk who quit his life as a soldier to become an s-class investigator. Practitioners of this methodology are tougher and more combat savvy than other s-class investigators.

links.title: Empiricism
links.snippet: Empirical studies are methods of investigation tried and true over many generations. These s-class investigators rely on keen deductive reasoning and insight to solve cases.

links.title: Forensic Science
links.snippet: S-class investigators dedicated to forensic science may or may not also have a background in alchemy, but regardless, they are experts in the fields of medicine and physicology.

links.title: S-Class Magus Hybrid Studies
links.snippet: Hybrid studies are available to both standard and s-class magi. Alterations and replacements made to the standard magus when selecting a hybrid study as an archetype are listed at the beginning of each.

links.title: Greed S-Class Oracle Mystery
links.snippet: Oracles who draw their power from the greed of mortals use those gifts to aid the poor and downtrodden masses.

links.title: Severed Symbiant Variant Maturation Option
links.snippet: The following option trades out the benefits of the s-class symbiant’s maturation class feature. They can also be gained as archetypes of the standard symbiant or as major convergences.

links.title: Clone Symbiant Variant Maturation Option
links.snippet: The following option trades out the benefits of the s-class symbiant’s maturation class feature. They can also be gained as archetypes of the standard symbiant or as major convergences.

links.title: Blood-Bonded (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
links.snippet: The blood-bonded are veritus champions that form a strong attachment to their blood dolls. This allows them to create more powerful companions from their blood debt who can fight alongside them.

links.title: Blood-Born (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
links.snippet: The blood-born are veritus champions whose power manifested early in life, causing them to suffer as they were thrust out of the normal life they led. Most grew into spiteful adults, shunned by those who didn’t understand the gifts they…

links.title: Blood-Crazed (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
links.snippet: The blood-crazed are veritus champions who internalize their gifts, using their blood debt to empower themselves, becoming even stronger the more they devote.

links.title: Cold-Blooded (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
links.snippet: The cold-blooded are veritus champions who have seen the worst the world has to offer and decided to fight against it by never giving an inch. They are merciless killers that only give their opponents one chance, if any, to not make the…

links.title: Arcane School Powers
links.snippet: When you select your arcane school at 1st level, you also gain one of its associated powers. You gain additional arcane school powers at 6th, 12th, 18th, and 20th level.

links.title: Soul Exemplar (Soulforge Archetype)
links.snippet: Rather than wielding armaments pulled from the akashic record, these rare warriors and historians focus entirely on aligning themselves with the souls of ancient heroes and villains, drawing forth even greater power than their more…

links.title: Archetypes
links.snippet: Archetypes are a quick and easy way to specialize characters of a given class, adding fun and flavorful new abilities to already established adventurers.

links.title: Affector (Maniac Archetype)
links.snippet: Through rigorous practice affectors achieve a degree of control over their emotions that allows them to shape and modify their emotive blasts in unusual ways.

links.title: Boredom (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome by mental fatigue. Everything appears dull to you, and you cannot bring yourself to start or finish the most basic tasks.

links.title: Compassion (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome by strong feelings of compassion for all living creatures. You care deeply for the well-being of others and you couldn’t hurt a fly—even the most wretched fiend is worthy of your pity.

links.title: Confusion (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are confused and disoriented. You have a hard time making sense of the things that happen around you.

links.title: Courage (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You remain steadfast and resolute in the face of grave danger and strong opposition, even against overwhelming odds. Others perceive you as brave, bold, or even fearless, but to you it’s simply a matter of composure.

links.title: Curiosity (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are nosy and inquisitive. Whenever you discover a hidden object or an area with restricted access, you feel a strong urge to investigate, even if it might put you or your allies into danger.

links.title: Desire (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome by strong feelings of lust and passion. Deep inside you there is a powerful craving that cannot be satisfied.

links.title: Disgust (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You feel a deep loathing for yourself and the world around you. Everything appears sick and repugnant to you.

links.title: Envy (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are consumed by a gnawing jealousy. You always compare yourself to others, and you envy them for their beauty, wealth, reputation, or power. You secretly revel in the misfortune of those whom you regard as rivals and to whom you feel…

links.title: Fear (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You suffer from anxiety, paranoia, or panick. You scare easily, and anything remotely threatening evokes dreadful imaginations in your susceptible mind.

links.title: Fractured Soul (Maniac Archetype)
links.snippet: The fractured soul harbors different personalities within the same body and mind that surface when she raves.

links.title: Grief (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: Bitterness, loss, and sorrow wear you down. Nothing in this bleak world can alleviate your sadness. Your pain is the only thing that makes you feel remotely alive.

links.title: Hatred (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome with blind loathing against those who have wronged you. Whatever your foes may have done to earn your enmity, the time of reckoning has come, and you will make them pay hundredfold.

links.title: Joy (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome by excitement, happiness, and euphoria. Life is a song and you dance to its tune, restless, light-hearted, and frolicking.

links.title: Korybant (Maniac Archetype)
links.snippet: Korybants see their rave as a gift from their divine patrons, whom they honor with enraptured dancing while clashing their weapons against their shields.

links.title: Loneliness (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome by a profound sense of loneliness. Detached from your surroundings and alienated from your friends and allies, you are forced to face your true self.

links.title: Love (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are overcome by a deep affection for those that you care about. You tend to see things through rose-colored glasses.

links.title: Regret (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are bitter and contrite over your past failures and transgressions. You would give anything for the opportunity to make things right and to avoid the shame of your past mistakes.

links.title: Surprise (Maniac Mania)
links.snippet: You are filled with a childlike sense of wonder, as if a whole new world unfolds around you. You are prone to amazement, shock, and awe.

links.title: Temperamentalist (Maniac Archetype)
links.snippet: The temperamentalist’s powers are rooted in the doctrine of the four temperaments (choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic, and sanguine), according to which emotions are caused by an excess or lack of body fluids, the four humors (yellow bile,…

links.title: Annis (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: The annis hags are massive hags with iron claws and a penchant for spreading misery. Their family is the most dangerous in melee combat.

links.title: Blood (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: The soucouyants or blood hags are known for their deceit as much as their control over fire. Their paragon hag families command dangerous fire magic and treacherous illusions.

links.title: Bone (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Believing themselves masters of the undead, bone hags* are natural necromancers. They pass along that power to their families.

links.title: Cauldron Hag (Paragon Hag Archetype)
links.snippet: Focusing on chemical admixtures rather than witchcraft, the cauldron hag approaches magic in a completely different way.

links.title: Coven Mother (Paragon Hag Archetype)
links.snippet: Although covens don’t generally have formal leaders, it’s common for one hag to rise to the top. A few paragon hags are naturals at this role, gathering coven-mates to them with disturbing ease.

links.title: Focused Hag (Paragon Hag Archetype)
links.snippet: While most paragon hags are tightly connected to their soul focus, these hags define their power by the focuses they carry.

links.title: Green (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Of all the hags, green hags are the closest to nature and the natural world. Their paragon hag families can easily be mistaken for aging druids or retired rangers .

links.title: Moon (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Although moon hags* claim divine inspiration or even divinity, their gifts seem to leave the receiver unhinged from reality. Their families are marked by their fluid forms, strange blessings, and the trail of madness left in their wake.

links.title: Mother of Steel (Paragon Hag Archetype)
links.snippet: Some hags never truly discard the tools of humanoid weapons, focusing on steel or staff while allowing her natural weapons to atrophy.

links.title: Night (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Haunters of dreams, these dark hags capture the souls of the sleeping for trade on the outer planes. Their paragon hag families traffic with dark powers.

links.title: Sea (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Although many harshly judge hags’ appearance, the sea hags are considered sickeningly ugly even by other hags. Their families turn this revulsion to their advantage, along with their mastery of the sea.

links.title: Storm (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Crackling with electricity, storm hags are found anywhere they can ride the storm winds. Their families are blessed with power over lighting, rain, and wind.

links.title: Winter (Paragon Hag Family)
links.snippet: Embodying the power and hunger of the coldest nights, winter hags live among the drifts and glaciers of polar regions. Their families gain the winter hags’ terrible connection with cold and ice.

links.title: Desire
links.snippet: Daevas of Desire seek out servants whose lust for physical pleasures burns within them with an all-consuming ferocity. Wild hedonists, passionate lovers, men and women who make their living or spend their gold in houses of ill repute, even…

links.title: Dominion
links.snippet: Daevas of Dominion seek out servants who are driven by an unstoppable drive to impose order and rule on the world around them. Many daevics of Dominion are great kings or cruel tyrants, though whether that is a result of the powers granted…

links.title: Akasin
links.snippet: The akasin believes in becoming one with the forces of righteousness, harnessing the radiance of the universe to gain powers of light and healing.

links.title: Shakta (Guru Archetype)
links.snippet: Shakta are gurus that have dedicated themselves to meditation and working towards physical perfection in order to awaken and channel the cosmic energies of the divine mother that sleeps within themselves. This energy is called kundalini,…

links.title: Sineater
links.snippet: Gurus of this philosophy believe that there is a finite amount of sin in the world and use their abilities to draw it out of others. Some sineaters do this out of an inherent desire to bring peace to those they free from sin; others…

links.title: Vayist

links.title: Enlightened Monk
